title: Finite-level compact-support direct image commutes with restriction of scalars
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated morphism of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $c=(j,\bar f)$, $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, be a compactification of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]: $j$ an open immersion, $\bar f$ proper, $\bar f j=f$. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite commutative rings in which $\ell$ is invertible on $Y$ (for instance the reduction $A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]). For $W\in\{X,\overline X,Y\}$ let $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be restriction of scalars along the induced map of constant sheaves of rings $A_W\to B_W$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; it is exact, so applied termwise it defines a triangulated functor $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. Let $Rf^{c,A}_{!}=R\bar f^{A}_{*}\,j_!$ and $Rf^{c,B}_{!}=R\bar f^{B}_{*}\,j_!$ be the compact-support candidates attached to $c$ with coefficients $A$ and $B$ [def-weil-compact-support-candidate], built from the extension by zero $j_!$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and the derived direct image defined with K-injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Then there is an isomorphism of functors $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$

$$
 Rf^{c,A}_{!}\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\circ Rf^{c,B}_{!},
$$

natural in the argument, namely the composite of the identification $j_!\operatorname{Res}_\varphi=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi j_!$ (both are computed termwise on the underlying sheaves of abelian groups) with the isomorphism $R\bar f^{A}_{*}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\cong\operatorname{Res}_\varphi R\bar f^{B}_{*}$ of [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars] for $\bar f$. For composable ring maps $A\to B\to C$ these isomorphisms compose to the one for $A\to C$.
